title: AI Cost & Observability (CineSpine)
description: Spend and latency for the Gemini calls, from the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions. Every panel here except the cache ratio reads gen_ai_*, which the OTel meter provider pushes; the cache ratio reads cinespine_*, which is scraped from /api/metrics. Cost is estimated, not billed -- see the panel description.

list.name: price_in
list.label: Input price (USD / 1M tokens)
list.description: Applied to every model on this dashboard. Fine while the router only reaches for Flash-tier models (llm_router.FLASH_FALLBACK_MODELS); wrong the moment CINESPINE_GEMINI_PRO_MODEL is set and Pro-tier calls land in the same series.

list.name: price_out
list.label: Output price (USD / 1M tokens)
list.description: Output is priced far above input, which is why the split below matters.

panels.title: Estimated Spend (selected range)
panels.description: An estimate: token counts multiplied by the price variables above. Nothing in the codebase knows a price, and no metric here carries dollars -- Grafana's own AI Observability cost panels read gen_ai_usage_cost_USD_sum, which is emitted by the OpenLIT SDK this project removed. So this number moves when Google reprices and nobody edits the variable. Read it as an order of magnitude.

panels.title: Estimated Spend Rate by Model (USD/hour)
panels.description:
Each side is aggregated to gen_ai_request_model before the addition. Without that the two selectors differ on gen_ai_token_type, the binary match finds no partner on either side, and the panel returns an empty vector -- silently, and indistinguishably from no traffic.

15m windows because the OTel reader exports on a 60s interval; a shorter range than roughly 4 export intervals produces gaps rather than a rate.

panels.title: Tokens per Second by Model and Type
panels.description:
gen_ai_client_token_usage covers every google-genai call the app makes -- character inference, the camera-report vision reader, the multimodal extractor and the Wrap Rescue memo -- because the instrumentation wraps the SDK rather than each call site.

The cinespine_llm_tokens_consumed_total counter this panel replaced was hand-placed at two call sites and recorded total_token_count only, so it both undercounted the run and could not separate input from output.

panels.title: Model Call Latency (mean)
panels.description:
Wall time inside generate_content, per model. This is the one metric name shared with Grafana's packaged AI Observability dashboards, so those panels would populate here; their cost and token panels would not.

Mean from the cumulative sum and count, not histogram_quantile over rate(). p95 is the better question, and the wrong query at this volume: a demo makes a handful of calls, so the bucket counters are flat across any sensible rate window, rate() returns 0 for every bucket, and histogram_quantile of all-zero buckets is NaN -- a blank panel, indistinguishable from no traffic. Verified against a real run. Switch to p95 when calls are continuous enough for the buckets to move.

panels.title: Agent Run Duration (mean)
panels.description:
The agent dimension rather than the model one, recorded by ADK itself in google/adk/telemetry/_metrics.py. Answers 'which agent is slow' where the panels above answer 'which model is slow'.

gen_ai_agent_name is verified, not assumed: a real Wrap Rescue run emits gen_ai_agent_name="wrap_rescue_handoff_agent". ADK also adds error_type to failed invocations, which splits the series -- aggregating by gen_ai_agent_name alone folds failures back in on purpose, since a run that died still took time.

Mean rather than p95 for the same reason as the model latency panel: one agent run per demo leaves the bucket counters flat, and a rate-based quantile over flat buckets is NaN.

panels.title: Tool Calls per Agent Run
panels.description:
Mean tool calls per invocation. Read beside the duration panel: a slow agent with a flat tool count is waiting on the model, a slow agent with a rising one is looping.

Expect 0 for wrap_rescue_handoff_agent, and that is correct rather than broken. The ClickHouse MCP queries are driven by the app's own step loop; the ADK agent is only asked to write the memo, so it calls no tools. This panel becomes informative if tool use moves inside the agent.

panels.title: AI Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description:
The one panel on this dashboard still reading cinespine_*, because the GenAI conventions have no equivalent -- a cache hit never reaches the SDK, so instrumentation that wraps the SDK cannot see it.

That means it populates only where /api/metrics is scraped. It is a ratio rather than the two raw rates it replaced, which could not be compared by eye when hits and misses differed by an order of magnitude.
